### Clone and run the start-basic example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/getting-started.md

Clones the official start-basic example into a local directory using gitpick, installs dependencies, and starts the development server.

```bash
npx gitpick TanStack/router/tree/main/examples/react/start-basic start-basic
cd start-basic
npm install
npm run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Install dependencies and build TanStack Start

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/examples/react/start-next-migration/README.md

Run from the repository root using Node 24 or newer and pnpm 11 before navigating to the migration example directory.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm nx run @tanstack/react-start:build
cd examples/react/start-next-migration
```

--------------------------------

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Navigate to an example app directory and start its development server.

```sh
cd examples/react/basic
pnpm dev
```

### Run tests and build for start-basic-react-query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/guide/tanstack-query.md

```sh
cd examples/react/start-basic-react-query

pnpm test:e2e
pnpm build
QUERY_EXAMPLE_PRODUCTION=1 pnpm test:e2e
```

### Configure and Run Start Script in package.json

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/examples/solid/start-bun/README.md

Adds the start script to `package.json` and runs it to start the production server.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "start": "bun run server.ts"
  }
}
```

```bash
bun run start
```

### TanStack Start server route handler with createFileRoute GET

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/lifecycle/migrate-from-nextjs/SKILL.md

Equivalent TanStack Start server route at src/routes/api/users.ts, defining the GET handler under the server.handlers option of createFileRoute.

```ts
// src/routes/api/users.ts
import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'

export const Route = createFileRoute('/api/users')({
  server: {
    handlers: {
      GET: async () => {
        const users = await db.users.findMany()
        return Response.json(users)
      },
    },
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure global request middleware in src/start.ts

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/react-start/SKILL.md

Create a start instance with createStart and register request middleware. The example logs each request method and URL before passing control to the next middleware.

```tsx
import { createStart, createMiddleware } from '@tanstack/react-start'

const requestLogger = createMiddleware().server(async ({ next, request }) => {
  console.log(`${request.method} ${request.url}`)
  return next()
})

export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({
  requestMiddleware: [requestLogger],
}))
```

### Install Netlify Vite plugin for TanStack Start

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/guide/hosting.md

Install the official Netlify Vite plugin as a development dependency. It configures the build for Netlify and emulates the Netlify production platform during local development.

```bash
npm install --save-dev @netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start
# or...
pnpm add --save-dev @netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start
# or yarn, bun, etc.
```

### Basic Client-Only QueryClient Setup in Router Context

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-router/skills/compositions/router-query/SKILL.md

Creates a QueryClient and passes it via router context, wrapping the router with QueryClientProvider. The root route must be created with createRootRouteWithContext (see the Root Route with Context example).

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import {
  RouterProvider,
  createRouter,
  createRootRouteWithContext,
} from '@tanstack/react-router'
import { routeTree } from './routeTree.gen'

// Root route declares that router context includes queryClient
// (root route file creates it with createRootRouteWithContext — see below)

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

const router = createRouter({
  routeTree,
  defaultPreloadStaleTime: 0, // Let Query manage caching
  context: { queryClient },
  Wrap: ({ children }) => (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>
  ),
})

declare module '@tanstack/react-router' {
  interface Register {
    router: typeof router
  }
}

function App() {
  return <RouterProvider router={router} />
}
```

### Inspect sample server startup output

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/examples/react/start-bun/README.md

Displays the console log output showing preloaded and on-demand assets at startup.

```txt
📦 Loading static assets from ./dist/client...
   Max preload size: 5.00 MB
   Include patterns: *.js,*.css,*.woff2

📁 Preloaded into memory:
   /assets/index-a1b2c3d4.js           45.23 kB │ gzip:  15.83 kB
   /assets/index-e5f6g7h8.css           12.45 kB │ gzip:   4.36 kB

💾 Served on-demand:
   /assets/vendor-i9j0k1l2.js          245.67 kB │ gzip:  86.98 kB

✅ Preloaded 2 files (57.68 KB) into memory
ℹ️  1 files will be served on-demand (1 too large, 0 filtered)

🚀 Server running at http://localhost:3000
```

--------------------------------

### TanStack Start route loader with createServerFn and Route.useLoaderData

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/lifecycle/migrate-from-nextjs/SKILL.md

TanStack Start route using an isomorphic loader that calls a GET createServerFn, with the component reading data via Route.useLoaderData().

```tsx
// src/routes/posts.tsx
import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'
import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'

const getPosts = createServerFn({ method: 'GET' }).handler(async () => {
  return db.posts.findMany()
})

export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts')({
  loader: () => getPosts(), // loader is isomorphic, getPosts runs on server
  component: PostsPage,
})

function PostsPage() {
  const posts = Route.useLoaderData()
  return <PostList posts={posts} />
}
```

```text
/devjokes
├── src/
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── demo/                         # Demo routes
│   │   ├── __root.tsx                    # Root layout
│   │   └── index.tsx                     # Home page
│   ├── components/                       # Solid components
│   ├── data/                             # Data files
│   ├── router.tsx                        # Router configuration
│   ├── routeTree.gen.ts                  # Generated route tree
│   └── styles.css                        # Global styles
├── public/                               # Static assets
├── vite.config.ts or rsbuild.config.ts   # TanStack Start configuration
├── package.json                          # Project dependencies
└── tsconfig.json                         # TypeScript configuration
```

### Configure Netlify netlify.toml for TanStack Start SSR

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/router/how-to/deploy-to-production.md

Set up build directories, Netlify functions, and redirect rules for TanStack Start server-side rendering support.

```toml
[build]
  publish = ".output/public"
  command = "npm run build"

[functions]
  directory = ".output/server"

[[redirects]]
  from = "/api/*"
  to = "/.netlify/functions/server"
  status = 200

[[redirects]]
  from = "/*"
  to = "/index.html"
  status = 200
```

Template prompt specifying instructions, structural requirements, and file updates for creating new how-to guides.

```markdown
Create a comprehensive how-to guide for [GUIDE_TITLE] following the established pattern:

1. **Read the priority document** at how-to-guides-implementation-plan.md for context
2. **Check existing documentation** mentioned in the Context section
3. **Follow the structure** from deploy-to-production.md:
   - Quick Start
   - Platform/scenario-specific instructions
   - Production checklist (if applicable)
   - Common Problems
   - Common Next Steps (commented out)
   - Related Resources (specific only)
4. **Update the README** at docs/router/framework/react/how-to/README.md
5. **Update tracking** in how-to-guides-implementation-plan.md
6. **Cross-reference existing guides** by uncommenting relevant "Common Next Steps"

Focus on practical, copy-paste ready solutions that solve real developer pain points.
```

### Access router instance with useRouter

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-router/skills/react-router/SKILL.md

Use useRouter to get the router instance directly, for example to call router.invalidate() to refresh data.

```tsx
import { useRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'

function InvalidateButton() {
  const router = useRouter()
  return <button onClick={() => router.invalidate()}>Refresh data</button>
}
```

### Configure vite.config.ts with TanStack Start and Solid

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/solid/build-from-scratch.md

Configure Vite plugins for TanStack Start and Solid. Note that vite-plugin-solid must be placed after tanstackStart.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/solid-start/plugin/vite'
import viteSolid from 'vite-plugin-solid'

export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    port: 3000,
  },
  resolve: {
    tsconfigPaths: true,
  },
  plugins: [
    tanstackStart(),
    // solid's vite plugin must come after start's vite plugin
    viteSolid({ ssr: true }),
  ],
})
```

### Implement In-Memory Error Reporting and Server Endpoint

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/guide/observability.md

Tracks reported errors in an in-memory Map and exposes them via a TanStack Start server GET handler on an admin route.

```tsx
// utils/error-reporter.ts
const errorStore = new Map<
  string,
  { count: number; lastSeen: Date; error: any }
>()

export function reportError(error: Error, context?: any) {
  const key = `${error.name}:${error.message}`
  const existing = errorStore.get(key)

  if (existing) {
    existing.count++
    existing.lastSeen = new Date()
  } else {
    errorStore.set(key, {
      count: 1,
      lastSeen: new Date(),
      error: {
        name: error.name,
        message: error.message,
        stack: error.stack,
        context,
      },
    })
  }

  // Log immediately
  console.error('[ERROR REPORTED]:', {
    error: error.message,
    count: existing ? existing.count : 1,
    context,
  })
}

// Error reporting endpoint
// routes/errors.ts
export const Route = createFileRoute('/admin/errors')({
  server: {
    handlers: {
      GET: async () => {
        const errors = Array.from(errorStore.entries()).map(([key, data]) => ({
          id: key,
          ...data,
        }))

        return Response.json({ errors })
      },
    },
  },
})
```

### Directory structure comparison between Next.js and TanStack Start

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/migrate-from-next-js.md

Compares the file and directory layout between a Next.js App Router application and TanStack Start with Vite.

```text
next-app/                 # Before: Next.js App Router
  app/
    layout.tsx
    page.tsx
    posts/[slug]/page.tsx
    actions.ts
src/                      # After: TanStack Start
  router.tsx
  routes/
    __root.tsx
    index.tsx
    posts.$slug.tsx
  server/account.ts
vite.config.ts
```

### TanStack Start file route with $postId param and Route.useParams

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/lifecycle/migrate-from-nextjs/SKILL.md

Equivalent TanStack Start route file. Dynamic segments use $param, and params are read via Route.useParams() instead of component props.

```tsx
// src/routes/posts/$postId.tsx
import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'

export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts/$postId')({
  component: PostPage,
})

function PostPage() {
  const { postId } = Route.useParams()
  // ...
}
```

### TanStack Start project directory structure

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/tutorial/fetching-external-api.md

Visualizes the expected folder and file layout for the movie discovery application.

```text
/movie-discovery
├── src/
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── __root.tsx                    # Root layout
│   │   ├── index.tsx                     # Home page
│   │   └── fetch-movies.tsx              # Movie fetching route
│   ├── types/
│   │   └── movie.ts                      # Movie type definitions
│   ├── router.tsx                        # Router configuration
│   ├── routeTree.gen.ts                  # Generated route tree
│   └── styles.css                        # Global styles
├── public/                               # Static assets
├── vite.config.ts or rsbuild.config.ts    # TanStack Start configuration
├── package.json                          # Project dependencies
└── tsconfig.json                         # TypeScript configuration

```

### Update package.json scripts for Vite dev, build, and start

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/lifecycle/migrate-from-nextjs/SKILL.md

Sets "type": "module" and replaces Next.js scripts with Vite equivalents. The start script runs the built server at .output/server/index.mjs.

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite dev",
    "build": "vite build",
    "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Setting up execution boundaries with TanStack Start functions

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/react/guide/code-execution-patterns.md

Defines server functions, server-only utilities, client-only utilities, and isomorphic functions using TanStack Start APIs.

```tsx
import {
  createServerFn,
  createServerOnlyFn,
  createClientOnlyFn,
  createIsomorphicFn,
} from '@tanstack/react-start'

// Server function (RPC call)
const getUsers = createServerFn().handler(async () => {
  return await db.users.findMany()
})

// Server-only utility (crashes on client)
const getSecret = createServerOnlyFn(() => process.env.API_SECRET)

// Client-only utility (crashes on server)
const saveToStorage = createClientOnlyFn((data: any) => {
  localStorage.setItem('data', JSON.stringify(data))
})

// Different implementations per environment
const logger = createIsomorphicFn()
  .server((msg) => console.log(`[SERVER]: ${msg}`))
  .client((msg) => console.log(`[CLIENT]: ${msg}`))
```

--------------------------------

### createStart(optionsFactory)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/start/framework/solid/guide/selective-ssr.md

Initializes and configures a TanStack Start instance. Allows defining global application settings such as the default server-side rendering behavior.

```APIDOC
## createStart(optionsFactory)

### Description
Initializes and configures the TanStack Start instance with global options such as `defaultSsr`.

### Signature
```typescript
function createStart(optionsFactory: () => StartOptions): StartInstance
```

### Parameters
- **optionsFactory** (`() => StartOptions`) - Required. A factory function returning configuration options.
  - **defaultSsr** (`boolean`) - Optional. Sets the default SSR behavior across all routes. Defaults to `true`.

### Example
```tsx
import { createStart } from '@tanstack/solid-start'

export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({
  // Disable SSR by default
  defaultSsr: false,
}))
```
```

### TanStack Start request middleware in src/start.ts

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/lifecycle/migrate-from-nextjs/SKILL.md

TanStack Start equivalent using createMiddleware().server to check the cookie header and throw a redirect to /login, registered via requestMiddleware in createStart. The src/start.ts file must be manually created.

```tsx
// src/start.ts — must be manually created
import { createStart, createMiddleware } from '@tanstack/react-start'
import { redirect } from '@tanstack/react-router'

const authMiddleware = createMiddleware().server(async ({ next, request }) => {
  const cookie = request.headers.get('cookie')
  if (!cookie?.includes('session=')) {
    throw redirect({ to: '/login' })
  }
  return next()
})

export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({
  requestMiddleware: [authMiddleware],
}))
```

### Configure and Deploy to Netlify

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/start-client-core/skills/start-core/deployment/SKILL.md

Install the Netlify Vite plugin and add it to `vite.config.ts`. Deploy using `npx netlify deploy`.

```bash
pnpm add -D @netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite'
import netlify from '@netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start'
import viteReact from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [tanstackStart(), netlify(), viteReact()],
})
```

### TanStack Start route head for metadata

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/packages/react-start/skills/lifecycle/migrate-from-nextjs/SKILL.md

Use createFileRoute with a head function to set meta tags dynamically from loader data.

```tsx
export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts/$postId')({
  loader: async ({ params }) => fetchPost(params.postId),
  head: ({ loaderData }) => ({
    meta: [
      { title: loaderData.title },
      { name: 'description', content: loaderData.excerpt },
      { property: 'og:title', content: loaderData.title },
    ],
  }),
})
```
